The test image shows a tomato leaf with large dark brown to black necrotic lesions at the leaf margins/tips, surrounded by yellow/tan transition zones, with the rest of the leaf remaining green. The lesions are irregular and large.

Key observations:
- Plant part: leaf
- Large dark brown/black necrotic areas at leaflet tips and margins
- Clear yellow/tan halos surrounding the dark lesions
- Bilaterally symmetrical pattern on two leaflets
- No visible white powdery coating or fuzzy growth

Top candidates: Early Blight (dark brown lesions with yellow halos), Late Blight (irregular dark brown patches), or Tomato Spotted Wilt Virus (necrotic spots with bronzing).

The large dark lesions with prominent yellow halos at leaf margins most strongly suggest Early Blight. Let me confirm with a reference image.

The reference Early Blight image shows a dark brown lesion with concentric rings (target-spot pattern) on a tomato leaf, which is characteristic of Alternaria early blight. 

Comparing to the test image:
- Test image shows large dark brown/black lesions at leaflet tips/margins with yellow halos
- Early Blight typically shows dark brown concentric ring lesions with yellow halos
- The dark coloration and yellow surrounding zones match well
- The location at leaf margins/tips is consistent with early blight progression

The test image aligns with Early Blight - the large dark lesions with clear yellow halos are the hallmark of Alternaria solani infection. The lesions appear slightly at the margins, which is common as early blight progresses on older leaves.
